analysis.title: Weekly HF Highlights: US L/S Net Lev Declines 8% WoW, HF De-Grossing Persists (Nov 6, 2026)
key_insights: US L/S net leverage fell 5% on Thursday Nov 5 alone to 42%, the 5th largest single-day decline on record since 2010. Nets are about 8% lower WoW and at the lowest level this year, but still above the roughly 35% lows of April 2025.

US L/S gross leverage ended at 202% (-4% WoW, 87th percentile since 2010) and is pushing toward 12-month troughs. HFs used Wednesday's relief rally to de-gross both longs and shorts, and this continued into a broad long-side supply event on Thursday.
The midterm elections cleared a political overhang but did not lead HFs to re-risk. Net selling on the day after the election replaced the record de-grossing stretch of July to October.

L/S gross flow over the past few months amounts to -10.7% of global GMV (gross market value) at end of June. MS says positioning imbalances across most sectors, factors and themes are now at moderate levels, and HFs no longer appear to be driving sharp equity reversals.

AI themes (Hyperscalers, Tech Beneficiaries and Power) are still about 32% of total US net exposure, down from 47% at the June peak. HFs are about 2% underweight these names relative to market cap weight, yet AI weakness still hit long books.

Over the trailing 4 weeks HFs covered shorts and softened underweights in the areas that rallied most, and cut longs in the areas that sold off most. Positioning was therefore lighter in the themes that moved most between Wednesday and Thursday.

The average US-based L/S fund lost 72bps in the first days of November, with Thursday at -1.6%. It took less than 30% of the S&P's losses on the day. YTD the average US L/S fund is +5.7% vs S&P 500 +8.4%, and about 35-40% of the cohort is flat to negative YTD.

MS says HF positioning is not extreme enough to trigger a sharp equity move on its own, but HFs can accelerate moves in both directions. They are sensitive to further losses and quick to sell weakness, and their very light positioning could also support an upside move.
US L/S net leverage is in the bottom decile of the last decade, which has historically been associated with more positive forward S&P returns.

APAC saw meaningful de-grossing in well-owned AI trades in Taiwan, South Korea and Hong Kong. Japan saw gross reductions concentrated in Tech, with a smaller share of long-side capital rotated into Discretionary and Financials.
EU HFs unwound longs in Tech, Energy and Health Care while covering shorts across Consumer. EU remains the smallest share of global gross exposure versus its 15-year history.

Regional leverage as of Nov 5: US gross 202% and net 42% (net at the 8th percentile since 2010). Europe gross 174% and net 53% (net at the 89th percentile since 2010). Asia gross 124% and net 51% (net at the 32nd percentile since 2010).
Asia-based L/S funds are up +4.4% YTD vs MSCI Asia +14.5%. EU-based L/S funds are up +1.5% YTD, lagging the SXXP at +13.9%.

Crowding: the Top 50 crowded longs lost about 8.54% in the week to Nov 5 vs about 5.28% for the Top 50 shorts, a spread of -3.25% against a -2.98% S&P move. On Nov 5 alone the crowded longs fell 7.49% and the crowded shorts 5.95%, while the S&P 500 total return was -4.36%. The YTD crowded long-short spread is still +11.27%.
risk_factors: HFs are sensitive to further losses and can sell quickly into additional weakness.
Continued long-side supply from de-grossing, as seen on Thursday, could extend equity declines.
Challenged HF performance YTD, with about 35-40% of US L/S funds flat to negative, may keep risk appetite low.
AI-linked long books remain vulnerable to further weakness despite lighter positioning.
vol_and_positioning: US L/S net leverage 42% (8th percentile since 2010, 0th percentile on a 1-year view, 12th on a 5-year view). Gross 202% (87th percentile since 2010).
Thursday's net leverage drop of 5% was the 5th largest single-day decline since 2010.
AI theme share of US net exposure fell from 47% in June to about 32%. HFs are about 2% underweight relative to market cap weight.
Top 50 crowded longs underperformed the Top 50 shorts by 3.25% MTD and WTD. The WTD spread z-score for N. America was -2.73.
Europe net leverage (53%) sits at the 89th percentile since 2010 while US net leverage sits at the 8th percentile.
MS flags bottom-decile US net leverage as historically associated with positive forward S&P returns.
geopolitical: US midterm elections cleared a long-awaited political overhang, but the outcome did not lead HFs to re-risk.

tension_points.bull_case: US L/S net leverage at 42% is in the bottom decile of the last decade, which has historically preceded more positive forward S&P returns. HFs are described as exceptionally supportive of an upside move given the extremely light positioning.
tension_points.bear_case: HFs are sensitive to additional losses and can be quick to sell into further weakness. De-grossing continued after the midterms and into a broad long-side supply event, and YTD PnL is challenged, with about 35-40% of US L/S funds flat to negative.
